title: Tips and tricks for artifact-free PFA-based fixation of the actin cytoskeleton and its regulatory proteins for single molecule localization super-resolution microscopy
protocol: Dissolve 2.5 g of BSA in 50 ml PBS.
Dissolve 2.5 g of glucose in 10 ml PBS.
Filter-sterilize the glucose solution and store at 4°C.
Dissolve 4.5 g of Glucose in 50 ml ddH2O.
Filter-sterilize the glucose solution and store at 4°C.
Dissolve 5 mg of glucose oxidase (60% purity) in 1 ml PBS.
Add drops of NaOH to dissolve EGTA until pH reaches 8.
Dissolve 9.51 g of EGTA in 50 ml ddH2O.
Mix 5 PBS tablets in 1 l of ddH2O, adjusting the pH to 7.4.
Filter-sterilize the PBS solution and store at room temperature for up to 6 months.
Mix 5 PBS tablets, 110.98 mg CaCl2, and 47.6 mg MgCl2 in 1 l of ddH2O, adjusting the pH to 7.4.
Filter-sterilize the PBS++ solution and store at room temperature for up to 6 months.
Dissolve Gelatin to a concentration of 0.5% (w/v) in PBS.
Autoclave the gelatin solution.
Aliquot the autoclaved solution into filter-sterilized 50 ml aliquots.
Store the gelatin solution at 4°C for up to 6 months.
Weigh 20 g of paraformaldehyde inside a fume hood.
Dissolve paraformaldehyde in approximately 50 ml of ddH2O.
Stir the mixture slowly on a hot plate, maintaining temperature below 55-57°C.
Add drops of NaOH until all paraformaldehyde is dissolved.
Adjust pH to 7.2 using HCl once the solution clears.
Adjust final volume to 100 ml with ddH2O.
Store the paraformaldehyde solution in filter-sterilized 5 ml aliquots at -20°C for up to a year.
Dissolve 15.12 g of PIPES in 50 ml of ddH2O.
Check and adjust pH to 6.8 if necessary.
Adjust final volume to 100 ml.
Filter-sterilize the solution.
Store PIPES aliquots at -20°C.
Dissolve 0.61 g of MEA in 5 ml of PBS.
Adjust pH with NaOH to 8.
Adjust total volume to 10 ml.
Stock MEA aliquots at -20°C for up to a year.
Dissolve 0.98 g of MES buffer in 25 ml of ddH2O.
Adjust pH to 6.1.
Add ddH2O up to 50 ml.
Filter-sterilize the solution.
Store MES solution at 4°C.
Dissolve 48 mg of MgCl2 in 10 ml for a 50 mM solution.
Filter-sterilize the MgCl2 solution and store at room temperature.
Dissolve 0.01 g of NaBH4 in 10 ml PBS to prepare a 0.1% (w/v) solution.
Prepare fresh NaBH4 solution before use.
Dissolve 11.7 g of NaCl in 50 ml ddH2O for a 4 M solution.
Filter-sterilize the NaCl solution and store at room temperature.
Place one coverslip of 24 mm in each well of a 6-well cell culture plate.
Wash coverslips with 2 ml 70% EtOH for 5 minutes, then rinse twice with PBS.
Coat wells with 1-2 ml of 0.5% gelatin solution and incubate at 37°C in a humidified incubator for 30 minutes.
Rinse coated coverslips twice with PBS++.
Seed 150,000 HeLa cells per well on freshly gelatin-coated coverslips two days before imaging.
Change the growing medium of the cells to DMEM supplemented with 0.1% FCS.
Leave cells in this medium for approximately 16 hours.
Stimulate cells with agonist of interest at the desired concentration on the day of imaging.
Observe cells under a phase contrast microscope after a few minutes to confirm response.
Prepare the appropriate fixation solution.
Warm up PBS++ to 37°C in a water bath.
Prepare two aliquots of cytoskeleton buffer by mixing stock solutions.
Add 1 ml MES (100 mM), 375 µl NaCl (4 M), 100 µl EGTA (500 mM), 100 µl Glucose (500 mM), and 1 ml MgCl2 (50 mM) to ddH2O up to 10 ml for each aliquot.
Add 0.3% glutaraldehyde and 0.25% Triton X-100 to one 10 ml aliquot of cytoskeleton buffer to prepare the first fixation buffer.
Add 0.5% glutaraldehyde to another 10 ml aliquot of cytoskeleton buffer to prepare the second fixation buffer.
Remove growing medium and rinse cells carefully with 2 ml of warm PBS++.
Replace PBS++ with the first fixation buffer.
Leave sample fixing for 2 minutes.
Remove first fixation buffer and add 1 ml of the second fixation buffer.
Incubate with the second fixation buffer for 8 minutes.
Rinse twice with 2 ml of PBS.
Remove PBS and add 0.1% NaBH4 solution for 10 minutes.
Perform all NaBH4 involving steps under a fume hood with proper protection.
Rinse twice with 2 ml of PBS for 5 minutes.
Fix cells at 37°C using PFA in PEM buffer.
Prepare PFA in stabilization buffer by mixing stock solutions and ddH2O.
Warm up PBS++ and PFA in cytoskeleton buffer to 37°C.
Remove the growing medium and rinse cells carefully with 2 ml warm PBS++.
Remove PBS++ and replace it with PFA in PEM buffer.
Leave the sample fixing for 10 minutes.
Rinse twice with 2 ml of PBS.
Remove the fixation solution and add 2 ml of 0.5% Triton in PBS for 10 minutes.
Rinse twice with 2 ml of PBS for 5 minutes.
Check the quality of the fixation using a phase contrast microscope.
Verify expected localization of fluorescent proteins tagged with FP using a fluorescent microscope.
Replace PBS from sample with blocking 5% BSA solution.
Allow BSA to block for at least 1 hour.
Alternatively, samples can be blocked at 4°C overnight.
Store samples at this point at 4°C for up to 1 week if needed.
Dissolve primary antibody in 100 µl of 5% BSA at an optimized concentration.
Incubate the coverslip facing down in a drop of 100 µl of antibody solution.
Incubate the sample for 45 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse twice with PBS.
Prepare a solution in 100 µl of 5% BSA with 0.6 U of Phalloidin and 10 µg/ml of secondary antibody.
Pick the coverslip with forceps and incubate facing down in a drop of 100 µl of staining solution.
Incubate the sample for 30 minutes at room temperature always protected from light.
Rinse twice with PBS.
Prepare the imaging buffer by mixing 200 µl of glucose prepared previously at 0.25 g/ml, 83 µl of Glucose Oxidase, 50 µl of MEA, and 6.75 µl of a 1:10 dilution of concentrated Catalase.
Add PBS to the mixture up to a final volume of 500 µl.
Clean the bottom of the coverslip thoroughly with 70% ethanol.
Wipe carefully in the same direction to avoid smudges and let dry.
Let dry.
Add 500 μl of imaging buffer to the sample holder.
Clean the objective with a 50-50 petroleum ether – butanol solution using a lens paper, wiping always in the same direction.
Let dry.
Let the sample holder stabilize for approximately 5 minutes before imaging.
Image the sample with the microscope.
Select the desired imaging setting.
Use TIRF option to image close to the basal membrane.
Choose EPI fluorescence option for actin in the cytoplasm or ruffles.
Excite cells with the appropriate laser/filter combination at high laser power in EPI mode.
Transfer molecules to the dark state.
Image the sample using the appropriate method (TIRF or EPI) for the necessary time.
Compare the results of the negative control sample with the samples stained also with primary antibody.
